work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XIV. · § 14 — Obedience … § 17 — Duty to be paid even to the worst Parents

items.text: Obey your parents in all things lawful, unless their command goes against God's command.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 14
items.quote: Children obey your Parents in all things... unless where their commands are contrary to the commands of God

items.text: Do not give yourself in marriage without your parent's consent, for you are in their possession.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 15
items.quote: Children are so much the goods, the possessions of the Parent, that they cannot without a kind of theft, give away themselves

items.text: Minister to them in all their wants—weakness, sickness, failing understanding, or poverty—according to your ability.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 16
items.quote: assist, and minister to them in all their wants of what kind soever, whether weakness, and sickness of body, decayedness of understanding, or poverty

items.text: If their command is against God's, refuse it, but do it with such modesty and respect that it appears conscience, not stubbornness.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 14
items.quote: he should take care to do it in such a modest, and respectful manner, that it may appear 'tis conscience onely, and not stubborness moves him to it.

items.text: Pay your duty to them even if they are harsh or wicked, for it is grounded in God's command, not their deserving.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 17
items.quote: no unkindness, no fault of the Parent can acquit the child of this duty

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XIV. · § 23 — To give them good example … § 25 — To give no unreasonable commands

items.text: Give them good example: live Christianly before them, that your example may win them to virtue.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV § 23
items.quote: he is not only to set him rules of vertue, and godliness; but he must himself give him a pattern in his own practice

items.text: Bless them by daily and earnest prayer, commending them to God's protection and blessing for their spiritual and temporal estate.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV § 24
items.quote: they are by daily and earnest prayers to commend them to Gods protection and blessing, both for their spiritual and temporal estate

items.text: By your own piety be such a person as that a blessing may descend from you upon your posterity.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV § 24
items.quote: by their piety they are to be such persons themselves as that a blessing may descend from them upon their posterity

items.text: Use your power over them with equity and moderation; give no unreasonable commands, but consider their real good.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV § 25
items.quote: parents must take heed, that they use their power over their children with equity, and moderation, not to oppress them with unreasonable commands

items.text: In arranging marriage, do not force them against their inclinations; choose a virtuous and pious person and regard their mutual liking.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV § 25
items.quote: they force them to marry utterly against their own inclinations, which is a great tyranny

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XIV. · § 18 — To Nourish them … § 19 — Educate them

items.text: Nourish and sustain him from birth until he can sustain himself.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 18
items.quote: the care of nourishing and sustaining it, which begins from the very birth, and continues a duty from the Parent, till the child be able to perform it to himself

items.text: Give suck yourself unless sickness, weakness, or like impediment; do not omit from sloth or niceness.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 18
items.quote: where no impediment of sickness, weakness, or the like does happen, 'tis surely best for the mother her self to perform this office

items.text: Bring them early to Baptism, to wash off the stain of sin and give them right to its advantages.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 18
items.quote: the bringing them to the Sacrament of Baptism, thereby to procure them an early right to all those precious advantages

items.text: Train them up in the way they should go: teach God's commands, rewards, and punishments; season them with virtue and religion.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 19
items.quote: Train up the child in the way he should go... they are by little and little to be taught all those things, which God hath Commanded them

items.text: Bring them up to some honest employment or trade, to avoid idleness and provide an honest living.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV, § 19
items.quote: bringing them up to some imployment, busying them in some honest exercise, whereby they may avoid that great snare of the Divel, Idleness

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XIV. · § 11 — Duties to our natural Parents

items.text: Revere and respect them with humility and observance; do not despise or contemn them, even in your heart.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: we must behave our selves towards them with all humility, and observance, and must not upon any pretence of infirmity in them, despise or contemn them, either in outward behaviour, or so much as inwardly in our hearts.

items.text: Cover and conceal their infirmities; do not publish or mock them.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: If indeed they have infirmities, it must be our business to cover, and conceal them; like Shem, and Japhet, who while cursed Cham publisht and disclosed the nakedness of their father, covered it.

items.text: Hearken to their counsel and obey their directions; do not despise them when they are old.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: Hearken to thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when shee is old.

items.text: Love them with real kindness: desire all good for them and do nothing to grieve or disquiet them.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: we are to bear them a reall kindness, such as may make us heartily desirous of all manner of good to them, and abhor to do any thing that may grieve or disquiet them.

items.text: Express love in kind behavior: readily do what brings them joy and comfort, and avoid what grieves them.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: in all kindness of behaviour, carrying our selves not only with an awe, and respect, but with kindness and affection, and therefore most gladly and readily doing those things, which may bring joy and comfort to them, and carefully avoiding whatever may grieve, and afflict them.

items.text: Pray for them: ask God to reward their goodness with multiplied blessings.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: this love is to be exprest in praying for them. The debt a child owe to a parent is so great, that he can never hope himself to discharge it; he is therefore to call in Gods aid, to beg of him, that he will reward all the good his parents have done for him, by multiplying his blessings upon them.

items.text: Do not curse them or wish evil upon them, not even in your heart.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XIV. § 11
items.quote: He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death, Exod. 21. 17.

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. · § 7 — To sympathy with them … § 10 — Love

items.text: Submit to your husband in all lawful commands; if a command seems unwise, calmly show the inconvenience, but if he persists, obey.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. § 8
items.quote: Wives submit your selves to your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.

items.text: Keep yourself pure and chaste from all strange embraces; give no ear to any who would allure you.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. § 9
items.quote: she must keep her self pure and chast from all strange embraces, and therefore must not so much as give an ear to any that wou'd allure her

items.text: Manage the worldly affairs he commits to you for his advantage; do not deceive him or use his goods for uses he does not allow.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. § 9
items.quote: she must order them so, as may be most to her husbands advantage, and not by deceiving, and cozening of him

items.text: Love him, and with that all friendliness and kindness of conversation; be his help and comfort in health and sickness, wealth and poverty.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. § 10
items.quote: she is to endeavour to bring him as much assistance, and comfort of life, as is possible, that so she may answer that special end of the womans creation

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. … § 6 — To restore them after falls

items.text: Have united hearts and affections; show the greatest tenderness and kindness to each other, avoiding contention.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV § 6
items.quote: they partaking in a more especial manner, of each others substance, and therefore ought to have the greatest tenderness and kindness, each to other

items.text: Look on each other as parts of yourselves; do not quarrel or envy, but strive to advance and help forward each other's good.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV § 6
items.quote: look on them as parts of themselves, and then they wil never think fit either to quarrel with them, or to envy them any advantage

items.text: Extend kindness to all who have any nearness of blood to you.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV § 6
items.quote: that this kindness is in some degree to be extended to all that have any neerness of blood to us

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XIV. · § 20 — Meane towards the educating of children … § 22 — To provide for their subsistence

items.text: Encourage them when they do well with rewards and kind notice, and do not provoke or discourage them by harshness.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 20
items.quote: endeavour to make children in love with duty, by offering them rewards and invitations, and whenever they do well take notice of it

items.text: Correct them when encouragement fails: first reprove, then if needed use the rod, but do it timely, moderately, without rage, and make them see their fault.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 20
items.quote: correction must be moderate, not exceeding the quality of the fault, nor the tenderness of the child

items.text: After they are grown, still watch over their souls: observe how they practice what they were taught, and exhort, encourage, or reprove as needed.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 21
items.quote: the parent is still to watch over them in respect of their souls, to observe how they practice those precepts

items.text: Put them in a way to earn a living and provide for their comfortable subsistence according to your ability.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 22
items.quote: since he was the instrument of bringing them into the world, he is according to his ability to provide for their comfortably living in it

items.text: Do not defer all provision until after your death; give them a competent portion while you live.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 22
items.quote: afford them not such a competency, as may enable them to live in the world

items.text: Provide for them only with honestly gotten wealth; do not gather an ill-gotten estate as their portion.
items.citation: Whole Duty of Man, Part. XIV § 22
items.quote: that the parent get that wealth honestly, which he makes their portion

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. · § 24 — Constancy … § 29 — Masters owe to their Servants Iustice

items.text: Obey him in all lawful commands, readily and cheerfully, as serving the Lord.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV §25
items.quote: Servants obey in all things your Masters... with good will doing service

items.text: Be faithful in all things entrusted to you: serve honestly even when unobserved, and do not waste or steal his goods.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV §26
items.quote: not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity

items.text: Bear his rebukes patiently and meekly; do not answer back, and mend the fault.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV §27
items.quote: not answering again

items.text: Be diligent in the duties of your place; shun idleness, sloth, and disorderly company that would take you from his business.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV §28
items.quote: he must constantly attend to all those things, which are the duties of his place, and not give himself to idleness, and sloth

items.text: Give them the food and wages agreed upon; do not withhold what you owe them.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV §29
items.quote: the Master is bound to be just to them, in performing those conditions, on which they were hired, such are commonly the giving them food and wages

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. · § 11 — The faults of the Husband acquits not from these duties … § 17 — The vertue of the person the chief consideration in Marriage

items.text: Be subject to your husband even when he is at fault, and by gentle conduct win him if he disobeys the word.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §11
items.quote: Likewise ye wives be in subjection to your own husbands, that if any obey not the word, they may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.

items.text: When you must admonish him, do it with such softness that it appears love, not anger.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §11
items.quote: let it be with that softness, and mildness, that it may appear 'tis love, and not anger, that makes her speak.

items.text: Love your wife tenderly and cherish her as your own body, forbidding all harshness and roughness.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §12
items.quote: No man, sayes he, ever hated his own flesh, but nourisheth, and cherisheth it.

items.text: Be faithful to your wife's bed, as God requires it of you no less than of her.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §13
items.quote: This is by God as well required of the husband, as the wife.

items.text: Maintain and provide for your wife, letting her share in the good things God has given you.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §14
items.quote: He is to let her partake with him in those outward good things, wherewith God hath blest him.

items.text: If your wife is ignorant of things concerning her eternal welfare, instruct her as one nearer to you than all others.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §15
items.quote: The husband is to instruct the wife in the things which concern her eternal welfare, if she be ignorant of them.

items.text: Pray for each other and help one another in all good, especially for the soul.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §16
items.quote: Husbands and Wives are mutually to pray for each other, to beg all blessings from God, both temporal and spiritual.

items.text: Before marrying, choose as your spouse one who truly fears God, valuing virtue above wealth or beauty.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV. §17
items.quote: choose such a person, with whom they may have this spiritual friendship, that is such a one, as truly feares God.

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. · § 30 — Admonition … § 35 — Encouragement in well-doing

items.text: Admonish and reprove the servant in case of fault, especially in faults against God, being more troubled at the dishonor of God and the hazard of his soul than at your own loss.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.30
items.quote: admonish and reprove the servant in case of fault, and that not only in faults against them, but also and more especially in faults against God

items.text: Administer admonition and reproof in a due manner: with sober and grave speeches, not in passion and rage, so as to convince him of his fault and assure him of your desire for his amendment.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.31
items.quote: not in passion and rage, but with such sober and grave speeches, as may convince him of his fault

items.text: Set a good example of honesty and godliness before the servant, for without this your exhortations and reproofs will do no good.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.32
items.quote: set good example of honesty and godliness to his servants

items.text: Provide that the servant may not lack means of instruction and daily constant times of worshiping God by prayers in the family.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.33
items.quote: provide that his servants may not want means of being instructed in their duty, as also that they may daily have constant times of worshipping God

items.text: Give reasonable and moderate commands, not laying greater burdens on the servant than he is able to bear, requiring not so much work that he has no time for his soul.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.34
items.quote: give reasonable and moderate commands, not saying greater burdens on his servants then they are able to bear

items.text: Give the servant encouragement in well-doing, using him with bounty and kindness as his faithfulness, diligence, and piety deserve.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, XV.35
items.quote: give his servants encouragement in well doing, by using them with that bounty and kindness which their faithfulness and diligence and piety deserves

work: The Whole Duty of Man, Partitions XIV-XV: Of Duty to Parents and of Parents to C
heading: PARTITION XV. · § 18 — Unlawful Marriages … § 23 — Prayer

items.text: Do not marry one who is within the degrees of kindred forbidden by God, whether to yourself or to your deceased wife.
items.citation: The Whole Duty of Man, Partition XV, §18
items.quote: marries any that is within any of those degrees of neerness, either to himself, or to his deceased wife, which is as bad, commits that great sin of incest
